hook.title: Body and Clothes
hook.content: Hand, voet, hoofd are old twins. Shirt and broek show the two article patterns, and blauw shows the adjective -e: het blauwe shirt, de blauwe broek.

pattern.title: Adjective -e after a definite phrase
pattern.content: Het shirt is blauw (predicate, no -e). Het blauwe shirt (definite, -e). De broek is blauw; de blauwe broek. The -e appears when the adjective sits before a definite noun.
pattern.trap_note: Do not add -e to a predicate adjective: het shirt is blauwe is wrong. The -e belongs to the attributive position.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Hand, Voet & Het Blauwe Shirt):
exercises.target_answer: de hand, de voet, het hoofd, het shirt, de broek, blauw
exercises.meaning: hand, foot, head, shirt, trousers, blue
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Hand, Voet & Het Blauwe Shirt": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says: “My hand is warm.”?
exercises.explanation: “Mijn hand is warm.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Hand, Voet & Het Blauwe Shirt”.

It means: My foot is cold.
exercises.explanation: “Mijn voet is koud.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Adjective -e after a definite phrase.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: Do not add -e to a predicate adjective: het shirt is blauwe is wrong. The -e belongs to the attributive position.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Het shirt is blauw.” is word-for-word “The shirt is blue.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Adjective -e after a definite phrase.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
cues: It means: The trousers are big.
exercises.explanation: “De broek is groot.” reuses only material taught in “Hand, Voet & Het Blauwe Shirt” — Adjective -e after a definite phrase.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “De broek is groot.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Adjective -e after a definite phrase.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “The trousers are blue.”
twist.explanation: Predicate adjective: no -e. Before the noun it would be de blauwe broek.

summary.outcome: Describe body parts and clothing, and place adjective -e correctly.
summary.takeaway: Adjective -e is a position rule, not a gender rule.
summary.curiosity_teaser: That is the whole Dutch trail — every core, sprig and branch is yours.

hand.etymology_derivation: The same body word as English hand.

voet.etymology_derivation: English foot and Dutch voet are the same word.

hoofd.etymology_derivation: English head and Dutch hoofd are cognate; both lost sounds in different places.

shirt.etymology_derivation: A recent English loan; Dutch treats it as het.

broek.etymology_derivation: English breeches and Dutch broek are the same word.

blauw.etymology_derivation: French bleu gave English blue and Dutch blauw.
